newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana Nov foreign reserves up 36 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Botswana Nov foreign reserves up 36 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Botswana's foreign reserves stood at a provisional 17.90 billion pula at end-November, 35.6 percent up on November 1995, Bank of Botswana research director Jay Salkin said on Monday.

"Most of the increase - around 66 per cent - was directly due to the depreciation of the pula," Salkin told Reuters. The currency, valued against a basket in which the South African rand is dominant, has fallen 21.5 percent against the dollar over the period.
"The rest came from increased earnings on exports, especially diamonds," Salkin said. Diamonds are marketed in dollars.
No diamond export figures for the period are yet available.

Based on the 1994/95 import figures of 4.25 billion pula and the latest estimated population figure of 1.4 million, the reserves are equivalent to more than four years' import cover or 12,785 pula per head of population.
